mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate (measured as the 3-month change in FEDFUNDS) is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as lower rates compress discount rates and boost equity valuations.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS has declined over the prior 3 months, or the rank correlation between the FEDFUNDS change signal and 20-day returns is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate (measured as the 3-month change in FEDFUNDS) is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days, as lower rates compress discount rates and boost equity valuations in the short term.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS has declined over the prior 3 months, or the rank correlation between the FEDFUNDS change signal and 5-day returns is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A positive change in real GDP (measured as the quarterly change in GDPC1) is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days, as stronger economic growth supports corporate earnings and equity valuations.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in > 60% of instances where GDPC1 has increased quarter-over-quarter, or the rank correlation between the GDPC1 change signal and 60-day returns is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.5%, it signals a tightening monetary cycle that leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days, as higher rates compress equity valuations and increase borrowing costs.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5%, or the rank correlation between the FEDFUNDS threshold signal and 20-day returns is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate falls below 4.0%, it signals a tight labor market that may lead to inflation and rate hikes, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of instances where UNRATE is below 4.0%, or the rank correlation between the UNRATE threshold signal and 5-day returns is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When real GDP growth (GDPC1) exceeds 2% and inflation (CPIAUCSL) remains below 2%, it signals a healthy economic expansion without inflationary pressures, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in > 60% of instances where GDPC1 > 2.0 and CPIAUCSL < 2.0, or the rank correlation between the joint signal and 60-day returns is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a supply-constrained economy (INDPRO < 100), the S&P 500 tends to produce negative returns over the next 20 trading days due to the risk of stagflation and reduced corporate margins as production constraints drive up costs.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where INDPRO < 100, or the rank correlation between the regime signal and 20-day returns is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a demand-driven housing market expansion (HOUST > 1500), the S&P 500 tends to produce positive returns over the next 60 trading days as housing market strength signals a robust consumer economy and supports corporate earnings.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in > 60% of instances where HOUST > 1500, or the rank correlation between the regime signal and 60-day returns is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.
